name: python-patterns
description: Python principles: think contextually, not by default.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

ASK user for framework preference when unclear
Choose async vs sync based on CONTEXT
Don't default to same framework every time

Framework: API/microservices or AI/ML → FastAPI; full-stack/CMS/admin → Django; simple/script/learning → Flask. Ask: API-only or full-stack? Need admin? Team familiar with async?

async def: I/O-bound, concurrent connections, real-time, async frameworks. def: CPU-bound, unfamiliar teams, blocking libraries. I/O-bound → async; CPU-bound → sync + multiprocessing.
├── Mix sync and async carelessly
├── Use sync libraries in async code
└── Force async for CPU work
Async libraries: HTTP httpx; Redis aioredis / redis-py async; ORM SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Tortoise.

Use type hints for public APIs and domain clarity; inference is fine for local variables and one-off scripts. Use Pydantic for API models, JSON schema, FastAPI, and clear errors.

Structure by feature/layer:
├── routes/ (API endpoints)
├── services/ (business logic)
├── models/ (database models)
├── schemas/ (Pydantic models)
└── dependencies/ (shared deps)
Separate concerns (routes → services → repos); put business logic in service

name: python-patterns
description: Python principles: think contextually, not by default.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

ASK user for framework preference when unclear
Choose async vs sync based on CONTEXT
Don't default to same framework every time

Framework: API/microservices or AI/ML → FastAPI; full-stack/CMS/admin → Django; simple/script/learning → Flask. Ask: API-only or full-stack? Need admin? Team familiar with async?

async def: I/O-bound, concurrent connections, real-time, async frameworks. def: CPU-bound, unfamiliar teams, blocking libraries. I/O-bound → async; CPU-bound → sync + multiprocessing.
├── Mix sync and async carelessly
├── Use sync libraries in async code
└── Force async for CPU work
Async libraries: HTTP httpx; Redis aioredis / redis-py async; ORM SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Tortoise.

Use type hints for public APIs and domain clarity; inference is fine for local variables and one-off scripts. Use Pydantic for API models, JSON schema, FastAPI, and clear errors.

Structure by feature/layer:
├── routes/ (API endpoints)
├── services/ (business logic)
├── models/ (database models)
├── schemas/ (Pydantic models)
└── dependencies/ (shared deps)
Separate concerns (routes → services → repos); put business logic in services.

Use async def with async DB/HTTP and concurrency; def with sync DB/CPU work. FastAPI runs sync functions in threadpool automatically. Use dependencies for auth, testability, and cleanup (yield).

Errors: code, message, details; NOT stack traces (security).
Test unit business logic, integration endpoints, E2E workflows with pytest; use pytest + httpx/TestClient and pytest + DB. Use fixtures: db_session, client, authenticated_user, sample_data.
